review_notes: I read the whole of Frame.lean. I compared its step and run lemmas with the neighbouring files Internal.lean, Internal/OutputBounds.lean and WorkReadOnly.lean. The one clear duplication is the "cells beyond head + t are untouched" argument. It appears for work tapes in Frame.lean and again, almost line for line, for the output tape in Internal/OutputBounds.lean. The same `simp only [TM.step]; split; simp; Option.some.injEq` unfolding also appears in `reachesIn_input_eq_of_idlesInput` and in several Internal.lean lemmas. I treated that unfolding as routine, so I did not report it as a separate finding. The proposed lemmas have not been compiled. Both files import Internal.lean, so Internal.lean is the natural home for the shared lemmas. `Tape.write` and `Tape.move_cells` are in TuringMachine.lean. I did not check whether the `Tape.writeAndMove` definition unfolds as assumed, so the sketch carries a small risk there. I found no other repeated machinery in the file. The remaining proofs are short or differ in substance.

findings.declaration: TM.work_cells_ne_of_step / TM.reachesIn_work_cells_far (duplicated by output_cells_ne_of_step / reachesIn_output_cells_far_internal in Internal/OutputBounds.lean)
findings.excerpt:
rw [← hstep]
    simp only [Tape.move_cells, Tape.write]
    split
    · rfl
    · change Function.update (c.work i).cells (c.work i).head _ j = (c.work i).cells j
      rw [Function.update_of_ne hj]
findings.problem: The two-stage argument "a step only writes under the head, so a run of t steps with heads moving at most 1 per step leaves cells beyond head + t alone" is proved here for work tapes and re-proved for the output tape in OutputBounds.lean. The step lemmas are identical in shape: unfold `TM.step`, `split`, discharge the halted case with `simp`, `rw [← hstep]`, `simp only [Tape.move_cells, Tape.write]`, `split`, `rfl`, then `Function.update_of_ne`. Only the tape selector differs, `c.work i` versus `c.output`. The run lemmas are likewise the same induction. The zero case is `cases hreach; rfl`. The succ case takes a one-step head bound, applies the step lemma with `by omega`, and rewrites with `ih`. Any later input or other tape variant would copy this a third time. Any fix to the argument has to be made in both places.
findings.proposed_change:
Add two generic lemmas in Internal.lean, which both files import.
1. `theorem Tape.writeAndMove_cells_ne (t : Tape) (s : Γ) (d : Dir3) {j : ℕ} (hj : j ≠ t.head) : (t.writeAndMove s d).cells j = t.cells j`. Proof: unfold `writeAndMove`, apply `Tape.move_cells`, then `Tape.write`. Split on `t.head = 0`: the first case is `rfl`, the second is `Function.update_of_ne hj`.
2. `theorem reachesIn_cells_far_of_step {tm : TM n} (f : Cfg n tm.Q → Tape) (hcell : ∀ {c c'}, tm.step c = some c' → ∀ {j}, j ≠ (f c).head → (f c').cells j = (f c).cells j) (hhead : ∀ {c c'}, tm.step c = some c' → (f c').head ≤ (f c).head + 1) : ∀ {t c c'}, tm.reachesIn t c c' → ∀ j, (f c).head + t < j → (f c').cells j = (f c).cells j`. Proof: induction on `reachesIn`. The zero case is `rfl`. In the step case, use `ih` at `j` with `omega` and `hcell` with `omega`, then `rw [ih .., hcell ..]`.
Then rewrite the work uses:
`work_cells_ne_of_step`: after `simp only [TM.step] at hstep; split at hstep; · simp at hstep; · simp only [Option.some.injEq] at hstep; rw [← hstep]; exact Tape.writeAndMove_cells_ne _ _ _ hj`.
`reachesIn_work_cells_far`: `fun hreach i j hj => reachesIn_cells_far_of_step (fun c => c.work i) (fun hs hj => work_cells_ne_of_step hs i hj) (fun hs => (head_le_start_add_of_reachesIn tm (TM.reachesIn.step hs TM.reachesIn.zero)).2.2 i) hreach j hj`.
The output version in OutputBounds.lean becomes the same with `f := fun c => c.output`. Its head bound uses `output_head_reachesIn_bound`, which that file already uses. It is not private there, and it is in Internal.lean (line 210), so it is available to both files.
findings.benefit: The "cells beyond head + t" induction and the one-step write lemma are each stated and proved once. `reachesIn_work_cells_far` and `reachesIn_output_cells_far_internal` shrink to short instantiations. They differ only by the tape selector and the head-bound source, and that difference becomes visible. The output-tape copy is the only other user today. A change to the step semantics, such as how `Tape.write` treats head 0, then needs a single edit.
